title: ESR (sed rate)
what: This is a simple blood test. It shows how fast blood cells settle in a tube. It is a general sign of inflammation.
why: Usually together with a complete blood count: at a checkup, or for fever, joint pain, or weakness.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come the next day
tell_doctor: If you were recently ill or had a fever

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Best in the morning before eating, or a few hours after a light meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

steps: Blood is usually taken from a vein, sometimes from a fingertip
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 day. The lab will tell you when

faq.a: It is only a general sign. A cold, pregnancy, and age can raise it. Your doctor looks at it with other tests.

faq.q: Why does ESR stay high after an illness?
faq.a: It goes back to normal slowly, sometimes over several weeks. Your doctor will order a repeat test.

reminders.text: ESR blood test tomorrow. Best to come before eating. Water is fine.
